question: Can the Transformer's self-attention use relative position representations instead of absolute position encodings to improve translation?
hypothesis: Precise relative position information is not useful beyond a certain distance, so clipping the distance should not hurt and should allow generalisation to unseen sequence lengths.
contributions: Relative position representations added inside self-attention (to keys and values), shared across heads
Efficient implementation splitting e_ij into two terms
Framing as relation-aware self-attention over labeled directed graphs

method.summary: Adds learned vectors per clipped relative offset to the keys (compatibility) and values (output) in each self-attention layer of the Transformer, replacing sinusoidal absolute encodings. Trained on WMT14 EN-DE and EN-FR with tensor2tensor, base and big configs.

datasets.split: test newstest2014; dev newstest2013 for ablations
datasets.preprocessing: 32,768 word-piece vocabulary; batched by approximate length

training.batch_size: up to 4096 input and output tokens per GPU; approximately 25,000 source and 25,000 target tokens per batch

other.checkpoint averaging: none for base; last 20 checkpoints saved at 10 minute intervals for big
other.throughput: 7% decrease in steps per second vs baseline

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 4, length penalty alpha=0.6
inference.samples: single run per config; not stated

limits: Only machine translation tested; authors say a^V-free may not hold for other tasks ('further work is needed')
Generalisation to unseen sequence lengths is hypothesised but not tested
Single runs, no variance or significance reported; BLEU details not given
Learning rate value not stated; relative gains differ (1.3 vs 0.3 BLEU) without explanation
Only encoder-decoder with fixed config; clipping k differs between base (16) and big (8)

terms.definition: extension to self-attention to consider the pairwise relationships between input elements, modelling the input as a labeled, directed, fully-connected graph
maximum relative position considered, clipped to a maximum absolute value of k, giving 2k+1 unique edge labels

lineage.note: Transformer with sinusoidal encodings is the baseline
word-piece vocabulary and beam search length penalty

figures.caption: Example edges representing relative positions, or the distance between elements. We learn representations for each relative position within a clipping distance k.
figures.why: shows how offsets beyond k share one vector

code.snippet: z_i = sum_j alpha_ij (x_j W^V + a^V_ij); e_ij = x_i W^Q (x_j W^K + a^K_ij)^T / sqrt(d_z); a_ij = w_clip(j-i,k); clip(x,k)=max(-k,min(k,x))
